headline.headline: TWINS ERUPT FOR FOUR IN THE NINTH TO STEAL ONE FROM KANSAS CITY
headline.deck: Minnesota rallies from three runs down to stun the Royals at Target Field
headline.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- The Kansas City Royals carried a 3-0 lead into the bottom of the ninth inning Thursday night at Target Field and appeared to have the game well in hand. Then the Minnesota Twins happened. A four-run explosion in the final frame turned a certain loss into a 4-3 walk-off victory before 22,944 stunned fans, sending the Royals to a gut-punch defeat they will not soon forget.

Kansas City had built its advantage patiently, scoring two runs in the third inning and adding a third in the fifth while Minnesota's lineup produced nothing through eight frames. The Royals needed only three outs to escape with the win. Instead, the Twins strung together enough damage to push across four runs, capped by the kind of inning that shifts momentum in a divisional race and sends a clubhouse into bedlam. Cameron earned the win in relief, picking up the victory as the Twins' bullpen held Kansas City scoreless through the late going.

The comeback vaults Minnesota back into the thick of the AL Central conversation at a time when Chicago's White Sox are setting the pace atop the division. For the Royals, who led by three runs with six outs to go, the collapse raises serious questions about their bullpen's ability to protect a late lead. Minnesota's Ryan Jeffers was hit by a pitch from Lucas Erceg during the proceedings, a small detail in a night defined by the Twins' refusal to quit.

secondary.headline: CUBS CASH IN EXTRA INNINGS, SILENCE BUSCH STADIUM IN TEN
secondary.deck: Chicago scores twice in the 10th to beat St. Louis and keep pace in the NL Central
secondary.body:
ST. LOUIS -- The Chicago Cubs came to Busch Stadium and left with a 4-2 victory in ten innings Thursday, scoring twice in the 10th to silence 29,475 fans and hand the Cardinals a painful home loss. St. Louis had led 1-0 after two innings and the game remained close throughout regulation before the Cubs finally broke through in extras. Reliever G. Soriano earned the win, holding the Cardinals scoreless long enough for Chicago's offense to do its work.

The Cubs got a run in the fourth inning to tie the game at one before the Cardinals answered with a run of their own in the seventh to reclaim a one-run edge. Chicago tied it again in the seventh as well, setting up the extra-inning finish. A pinch hitter grounded out for Dean in the 10th after the Cubs had already seized control with their two decisive runs. The victory keeps Chicago competitive in the National League Central, where every game against a division rival carries extra weight with the calendar turning toward August.

secondary.headline: FÄRJESTAD RESCINDS FOOTE CONTRACT AMID SWEDISH FAN BACKLASH
secondary.deck: Swedish Elite League club bows to fan pressure and backs away from deal with Cal Foote
secondary.body:
Färjestad BK of the Swedish Elite League announced Thursday it will not honor the contract it had agreed to with defenseman Cal Foote, citing conversations with supporters who expressed strong opposition to the signing. The move is an extraordinary capitulation to fan pressure and places Foote in professional limbo at a sensitive moment in the hockey calendar, with the NHL playoffs still grinding through the second round and rosters beginning to take shape for the coming season.

The decision underscores the intensity of fan culture in Swedish hockey, where supporters wield influence that can reach into front-office decisions. Foote, whose NHL career has included stints with multiple organizations, had apparently agreed to terms with Färjestad before the deal unraveled under public scrutiny. The episode raises broader questions about player leverage and club accountability in European leagues, where contracts are sometimes treated as more fluid than their North American counterparts.

secondary.headline: SAMUEL HEADS BACK TO SAN FRANCISCO ON ONE-YEAR PACT
secondary.deck: Wide receiver Deebo Samuel returns to the 49ers on a deal worth up to seven million dollars
secondary.body:
Deebo Samuel is heading back to Santa Clara. The versatile wide receiver has agreed to a one-year contract with the San Francisco 49ers worth up to seven million dollars, according to sources familiar with the deal, ending what had been a brief stint in free agency. Samuel, known for his ability to line up in the backfield as well as outside, gives San Francisco a proven weapon as the club prepares for training camp and the 2026 season.

The reunion makes sense on both sides. Samuel knows the 49ers' offensive system and has produced big numbers in the scheme when healthy. San Francisco, meanwhile, avoids the uncertainty of replacing a player whose versatility is genuinely difficult to replicate at the NFL level. With several prominent free agents still searching for landing spots -- Joey Bosa and Stefon Diggs among them -- Samuel's quick return to the Bay Area stands as one of the cleaner resolutions of the offseason's lingering personnel questions.

column.headline: MINNESOTA'S NINTH-INNING MIRACLE SHOULD TERRIFY EVERY AL CENTRAL RIVAL
column.body:
Let's be honest about what happened at Target Field on Thursday night. The Kansas City Royals had three outs separating them from a clean road win, a comfortable three-run cushion, and every reason to believe the game was over. The Minnesota Twins had produced nothing for eight full innings. Nobody in that ballpark -- and nobody watching -- genuinely believed Minnesota was going to score four runs in the ninth. And yet. That is the kind of team the Twins quietly appear to be building, the kind that scratches back when the math says don't bother.

The AL Central is supposedly Chicago's division to lose, and the White Sox have earned that billing after stunning the Yankees in eleven innings this week. But a Twins team that can manufacture a four-run ninth against a respectable Royals bullpen is a club that deserves serious attention before the August trade deadline reshapes the landscape. Kansas City's bullpen will take the blame today, and fairly so. But give Minnesota credit for staying in the batter's box when lesser teams would have been watching the exits. That ninth inning should make every contender in the American League at least a little uneasy.

story.headline: WHITE SOX STUN YANKEES IN 11 AS CHICAGO BUILDS AL CENTRAL LEAD
story.deck: Headrick and Chivilli combine to silence New York in extras at Guaranteed Rate Field
story.body:
CHICAGO — The Chicago White Sox scratched out a 2-1 victory over the New York Yankees in 11 innings Thursday night, with a runner crossing the plate in walk-off fashion in the bottom of the 11th to send 29,384 fans home satisfied. The game was a scoreless deadlock through nine full innings before the Yankees pushed across a single run in the top of the 10th, only for Chicago to answer immediately with a run of its own to force an 11th. A pinch runner for Jazz Chisholm Jr. eventually scored the decisive run, capping a grinding, low-scoring affair that stretched 3 hours and 15 minutes.

Pitchers Headrick and Chivilli shared the winning decision for Chicago, which improved to 57-51 and retained first place in the AL Central. The Yankees stranded a staggering 26 runners on base, squandering chance after chance against a White Sox staff that bent repeatedly but never fully broke. Seuly Matias Dominguez doubled for New York, as did Austin Wells and Randal Grichuk, yet none of those extra-base hits translated into enough offense to secure a victory.

Elsewhere Thursday, the Tampa Bay Rays outlasted the Texas Rangers 3-2 at Tropicana Field as Jonny DeLuca hit his seventh home run and Cedric Mullins added his 13th for Texas, with the Rays scoring the decisive run on an eighth-inning rally. The Minnesota Twins rallied for all four of their runs in the bottom of the ninth to defeat Kansas City 4-3, with Nolan Clemens belting his 19th homer and Wyatt Caglianone adding his 17th as part of the late explosion. Those Twins, who enter today at 55-55, open a three-game series in Seattle looking to climb back to the .500 mark.

story.headline: OKPARA FINDS HOME IN D.C., BLAZERS SEEK MODA DEAL, AND PACERS UNVEIL THROWBACK THREADS
story.deck: Washington rookie Felix Okpara embraces Nigerian roots in the capital as the league buzzes with offseason moves.
story.body:
Felix Okpara has not played a single NBA minute yet, but the 22-year-old center already feels a deep pull toward Washington. The Wizards rookie, born in Nigeria, has drawn comparisons to Patrick Ewing in his imposing 7-foot frame and relentless post presence, and team officials say he has embraced the city's substantial Nigerian-American community with genuine enthusiasm. Okpara told reporters Thursday that walking the halls of Capital One Arena for the first time felt less like arriving at a job and more like arriving at a destination.

Across the league, the Trail Blazers took their arena future into their own hands Friday, sending team representatives into a formal session with Portland city councilors to negotiate a new lease and explore public commitment to a Moda Center revamp. The talks come as several franchises around the NBA have secured lavish new facilities, leaving Portland's 1995-era building looking increasingly dated. No dollar figures were confirmed publicly, but sources familiar with the discussions described both sides as motivated to reach an agreement before the 2026-27 season tips off.

Indiana added a splash of nostalgia to an already busy offseason by unveiling new Statement Edition uniforms that reach back to the pinstriped look the Pacers wore during their bruising late-1990s run, when Reggie Miller tormented opponents and Rick Carlisle's predecessor Larry Bird prowled the sideline. Meanwhile, the league's broader free-agency caldron keeps churning, with veteran scorer DeMar DeRozan still unsigned and drawing interest from multiple contenders. The summer of 2026 has given NBA fans plenty to digest before a single jump ball is thrown.

story.headline: CELEBRINI BECOMES NHL'S HIGHEST-PAID PLAYER AS SHARKS LOCK UP FRANCHISE CENTER TO $94M DEAL
story.deck: San Jose secures its future with a blockbuster extension for the 20-year-old phenom.
story.body:
The San Jose Sharks have made Macklin Celebrini the richest player in the NHL, signing the 20-year-old center to a five-year, $94 million contract extension Thursday that carries an average annual value of $18.8 million, surpassing every other skater in the league. The deal, announced at the NHLPA Rookie Showcase in Toronto, signals San Jose's full commitment to rebuilding around the former Boston University standout who instantly became the face of the franchise after being selected first overall in the 2025 NHL Draft.

Celebrini's extension arrives on the same day fellow top pick Gavin McKenna, the No. 1 selection in the 2026 Draft, set his own rookie-season benchmarks at the Showcase. McKenna, the 18-year-old Medicine Hat product, told reporters Wednesday he is targeting 30 goals and 70 points in his first NHL campaign, a declaration that drew comparisons to Celebrini's own rapid ascent. The two prospects represent the most hyped back-to-back top picks in a generation, and the league wasted no time putting both names in front of cameras.

The Celebrini signing overshadowed a pair of notable stories elsewhere in the hockey world Friday. The International Ice Hockey Federation confirmed Russia will remain barred from four major IIHF tournaments in 2027, continuing the organization's stance following the invasion of Ukraine. Meanwhile, Färjestad BK of the Swedish Elite League rescinded a contract offer to defenseman Cal Foote after a fierce backlash from the club's supporters, leaving the 26-year-old blueliner without a destination heading into the summer.

story.headline: VETERANS FIND NEW HOMES AS NFL FREE AGENCY RESHAPES ROSTERS AHEAD OF TRAINING CAMP
story.deck: Big names are on the move this spring as teams retool for the 2026 season.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has been anything but quiet, with several marquee veterans switching jerseys in a flurry of trades and free-agent signings that have scrambled the balance of power across both conferences. Offensive linemen and pass rushers have commanded the richest contracts, reflecting a league-wide premium on protecting quarterbacks and disrupting them in equal measure. Multiple rebuilding franchises have also used the spring to shed expensive veterans, clearing salary cap space and signaling a full commitment to youth movements launched during the April draft.

The 2026 NFL Draft drew significant attention for the depth of its quarterback class, with scouts and front offices debating for months which signal-callers possessed the tools to develop into legitimate starters. Several teams in the bottom tier of last season's standings moved aggressively to trade up and secure their franchise quarterbacks, setting the stage for position battles that will define training camp rosters come July. Meanwhile, analysts have pointed to an unusually strong group of edge rushers selected in the middle rounds as a potential source of breakout performers in the coming season.

With mandatory minicamp dates approaching in June, several high-profile holdouts and unsigned draft picks are creating headaches for front offices trying to finalize depth charts. Veteran wide receivers in particular have expressed frustration with the market, as team spending has skewed heavily toward the trenches. Coaches across the league have emphasized that early reps in camp will carry added weight this year, with new offensive and defensive systems being installed in Dallas, Cleveland, and New Orleans following a wave of coordinators hired away from college programs.
